agent.problem: The card begins with the first-person quotation "How I long for Your precepts!" and identifies the writer as the speaker only afterward. The speaker needs to be identified before the quotation.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

human.problem: Psalm 119 is an acrostic with eight-verse stanzas: verses 25-32 (Daleth), 33-40 (He) and 41-48 (Waw). The stops split at verse 34, so the He stanza is cut across two stops.
human.question: For Psalm 119, or other acrostic and stanza-based poetry, should stops follow the stanza boundaries? Here that would mean three stops of eight verses each. Or is any split that keeps stops short acceptable?
